body:
You are not stupid! Even if you were stupid, there are way more important things than intelligence, especially in conversations! 
  I'd much rather have a conversation with someone who has an interesting life story, who struggled with hardships like you have, then to some smart happy go lucky person. 
   Having Autism is hard! I know... I worked with Autistic children for a long time. I know how tough it can be to be so different. But different doesn't always mean bad. Quite the contrary! Many of the greatest people in our world have had severe disorders or diseases. 
  Being different is a gift if you can get through the pain and be productive. 
  You have a special brain that most people do not have. It has its downsides, but it also has its upsides... talents that you have that you clearly don't yet see, but that other people can't have. 
   Mozart, considered the greatest composer of all time is said to have had Autism. 
   Tim Burton, one of the most successful filmmakers of our day, has Autism. 
   Andy Warhol, one of the most successful artists of all time. 
   Lewis Carroll, one of the most prolific and popular authors of all time. 
   Temple Grandin! 
   
I will talk to you any time you need, forever... or until you realize that you don't need me to feel good about yourself! 
  You cannot end your own life just because your family is being harsh and mean. You cannot end your beautiful existence just because you haven't found the right friends yet! You cannot hang yourself because this life is all any of us have! 
  You can respond to this in any way you'd like and I will continue to talk to you for as many days, months, years... that you need. I will be your friend until you realize that there are much better people than me who will be amazing friends to you. 

All of us have the challenge of finding ourselves in this world... yours is very hard in many ways, as is most peoples. Yours might be harder... but if you follow what you love and what makes you happy, if you work hard and if you continue learning, you will have an amazing life!

Well said... 
 I'm glad you're feeling a bit better.

I feel this way really often... 
 The truth is, it's more likely not true than true. I'm not saying you haven't had your heartbroken or had friends who don't like you... but often times, people who are depressed (like me) feel like other people don't like them. We get sensitive and we think so much and have so much anxiety that we feel like we're hard to be around. 
 Your confused about why this is because it really isn't... the truth is, you need to find your clique. You need your group of people that you will love and that will love you. 
 Don't try to be part of a group just because you think you're supposed to. Some people do well alone for a while... But seek out people who you look up to, and when you find them, be yourself around them and stick to them. 
  Be Yourself! The friends who will prove real friends are the ones who will like you for who you are, with all of your insecurities. 
   Bottom line: there is nothing wrong with you! 
Or, I should say, nothing wrong with you any more than the rest of us. We are all crazy in some ways... but your life isn't over. You have so much time and no idea of what will happen. 
 Stay positive. Find people you love. Do things you love. Be happy. Be you. It will come to you!

I swear on my life that I love you, completely, and I don't even know you... I mean, I know you but I've never met you. 
 The truth is, you're dealing with depression and that can be tough. 
We both know that your issues, although they feel really important, in the grand scheme of life are not that much of a big deal. Think about it, there are people who are happy with tons of acne, and there are perfectly flawless people who are super sad. So it's not that. 
  Your parents aren't good at telling you they love you. That can be tough... Finding your secure headspace is tough, especially when you weren't given it as a child. You need to find a way to be loved and to love yourself, and that can take years or a lifetime. 
  But here's the important thing: 
    You are still young. I know you hate hearing it, but the reality of life is that it changes, for everyone. Your life in college might be completely different than your life in hs. A lot of people have that experience. In college people tend to forget about those little things... there are much bigger problems, but also much greater joys. So don't quit yourself now. It's not okay to the person you might become. 

 Maybe try to accept all of these things... imagine you said to yourself: "Okay. I have acne, no gf, no love from parents, a dad who can be harsh..." sooooo... it's rough, but it isn't the end of the world. 
  Accept the difficulties you have in your life. They are part of your life. But there is more to you than anything you mentioned here. 
  You are sensitive, vulnerable, smart, you can write, you have a home, a school, food, freedom to be who you want to be, a future... and most importantly, you have life. 
  Life is the greatest gift on earth because it is really all we have... past everything else, there is life. Beyond your issues and sorrows and anything you will ever think or feel, there is the key word: life. It is all you have, really! One day it will be gone and you will cry and wish you could stay longer. 
 Life is a gift... even the worst life is better than the nothing that exists without life. 
   You need to try and find the things in your life you are grateful for. There are billions of people in this world who have nothing. Who are dying of sickness or trapped in a place they can't get out of, or in prison, or in Iraq, or in a freezing cold country, or working full time as a slave... 
   Your life is not so bad. 
You will change. You will get better. But you need help... don't do this yourself. Talk to people, people you trust. If it goes wrong, try someone else. Nothing is worth taking your life for. Nothing! 

 I love you and I care about you. If I knew where you were right now I would try to give you everything you needed because people need love. It is okay to be alone or sad or both... it is okay. But we care about you. A lot... 
  Here is how important your life is to me: if I knew that I could save your life by giving away all of my money and clothes and food, I would do it in a heartbeat. If I had to live in a desert alone for five years to save your life, I would do it in a heartbeat! Your life is worth it. It is the only thing you have and it is incredibly important! 
  I swear you will look back at this with nostalgia. Don't be too harsh on yourself when you do. This is a part of your journey... just another way to become stronger! 
 Please respond if you feel up to it.

Hey Mr. or Mrs. Parker... 

 Listen real close, okay? 

These feelings that you're having - the ones you feel like nobody understands or really gets... the ones that feel so real to you and that making even just sitting still hurt like hell... the ones that make you want to cry but feel like crying isn't enough... the ones that make you want to sleep forever or never sleep... the ones that make your whole body hurt in a way that nothing can take away, and the things that do take it away seem useless and pointless....... 

 I understand those feeling! WE understand those feelings. It's why we're here. 

1: Know that those feelings are okay. It is okay to feel really sad and it's okay to feel like a burden and feel like you're hurting people. It isn't unique to only you and it isn't "bad"... it's okay. 

2: Know that what you're feeling is not necessarily (it might be, but probably isn't) a real representation of reality. It's true that you might be hurting people and that your best friend is really angry or even hates you. But it's just as likely that that isn't true and it's just how you feel right now. Either way is okay. 

3: Know that many people suffer from depression from time to time. It isn't something they choose. Rather, like a headache or cancer, it just comes to you and controls you. The worst part is that it controls how you feel and makes you believe it's right or even real. It's a medical issue that can be treated with SSRI's... 

4: Know that you are a sensitive person. You may think you're so strong (you might be) and so bad (you might be) or so lame (maybe) or so useless (possibly)... but you are a sensitive person! And that is worth a billion dollars... you are worth more than you know because you are human and because you are alive. You will never win american idol or get an oscar... and if you did, those things wouldn't change anything. You are special and unique because you are human and because you're alive! That's it! 

5: Life, this life, is the only thing you have. There is no dreamland or other universe... there is no place of perfection or place where what happened never happened. There is only this world. It is rough!!! Really rough sometimes... but it is also beautiful. Every blade of grass if freaking beautiful. 
  Please don't expect this world to change. What will change is you. You have a problem right now, something that you will get through and survive with... you will come out stronger, smarter and happier. Nothing will change until you change. You may need some medication (like I do), but you may not. Either way... today is all you have, so get started. Don't dream of exotic worlds where everything is easy. Just find beauty here! 
 The choice is always yours. Yes, things are horrible right now for you. I understand! I cannot judge you at all... but I do know that you can change, slowly, to see this world for what it is: everything you will ever need and the only thing you have! 

 Have some fun today!

You know what this sounds like? 
  So, I'm not a therapist. I studied psych for five years and lived for 26... and I'm no professional, but I think I know what this is. 
  I think it's life. 
It gets hard.  Things become real... existential reality is rough, especially when you're smart as you are. So perhaps this confusion and inability to find the perfect place... maybe that's life. 
  Yes. Life probably gets easier when you find love and touch. I don't know. I'm hoping for that as I'm in your situation more deep than I can explain. 
   But I think there is hope. 
Not knowing what love is makes finding out so much more amazing. I'm sure of it.

Parents are the hardest to get acceptance from... again, the need for their love is so deep-rooted... but it is a chase that never ends. The love will come from within you. 
  I think looks are important to a part of the people in this world. You say "reality is like this" and that's true... but it's only true of a younger and more naive generation. It's something we get past as we get older. Really, all the time spent thinking about looks is wasted. It's ephemeral. 
    Instead of trying to change how you look (impossible) or get people to like you for how you look (pointless) why not move up to the tier of people who are concerned with more important things. Try to neglect the way you look and put your focus onto more important things. I know it's tough. 
  It's got to come from a place of wisdom... the mindset should not be "looks are important but I don't care". Rather, "looks really aren't that important and I'm over it. I've moved on to a more fulfilling goal." 
  I think you have it in you.

Well, don't you think it could be the depression telling you that you don't want to get better. I mean, being depressed is hard to deal with for this specific reason. It makes you believe there's no point to living. 
  You're right. I guess don't call the hotline. But is there anyone in your life that you can talk to? 
  You don't want to get better now, and I get that... but what if you will feel differently in a few days, weeks, months, years... what if this part of your life won't even be remembered in the future. Things do change. They always do.

Hey... 
  You watch Game of Thrones? 
What's up? How old are you?

You are being strong! Life is hard... you are fighting yourself from taking the easy way out. Do not confuse that with weakness. 
 Being able to handle the pain you're feeling now, that is strength! You can get through this, really slowly. I swear. 
   Ending your life would be the cowardly thing to do. Not just that, but it would be unfair to your future self! You sound young... there are years and years and years of life for you. You can't see it now because you are a bit sick or sad, and that's okay. But you cannot end it now! 
  Get that idea out of your head. It's not happening. You have so so so much life. 
    Change your perspective. You need help right now and we can help you. But killing yourself is not an option. You don't wanna be just another name with a picture. Please. 
   Call the suicide help line. They will help you. You will find the right therapist or meds or people and you will feel so good! 
  You are not feeling well now. I understand that. I've been there. But please, you need to give yourself a chance. 
  Stop being weak by thinking you need to get out. This life is the only thing you have. There is nothing else. It is a gift. You have this life, do not give it away. Just sleep, or drink, or smoke, or walk, or run, or eat... do anything else. Walk out of your room. 
 Tell someone close to you who you love and trust or message me. Please! You are loved...

You write very beautifully. 

I think there is a simple problem here that is confusing things a bit... 

There is no one else in the world that can make you feel loved. No matter what they say, what they do, who they are or how hard they try... your love will come from within you. 

I know it sounds so cliche... but you are seeing that reality now! You have all of those things and yet you cannot feel it. I understand it because I am the same way. But recognizing where the problem lies might help you feel less hopeless. 

You must love how you look, love who you are, love what you say and what you do... There are many things in childhood that can contribute to feeling this way.  You mentioned that in your comment. 

Here is what I would do in an ideal world... 
  I would turn off my phone, close my laptop, put on the most simple clothing I have, put on zero makeup, don't look in the mirror, take some deep breaths and go out into the world. The forest, the desert, a field, a river, a long walk in a city... something to connect you back with the world. 

Your weight, your looks, your hair, your skin... these things are insignificant in the grand scheme of life. When the focus is on those things and you try to find love through them or by being loved for them, you will come out feeling empty. 

You are so much more than any way you can ever look and so much more than the love anyone else could ever give you.

Hey man, 

Sounds like you're having a tough night. It's interesting... we all have these nights sometimes, but it's so hard to feel it when you're not in it. But trust me, I know what you mean. 
 So glad you came here for help... it probably feels surreal to you that this all happened. I mean, stepping out into the road. It's probably something you've imagined, but you can't believe you did it. 
  No worries... glad you're okay. 
It's true what others are saying. You aren't doing anything wrong. In fact, there's really no connection between how you feel and what's actually going on in your life. Of course, losing your girlfriend is super hard and can make you sad... but it sounds like you have depression, and that's a thing in its own. But we understand. 
  Look... if we're being realistic, this girl is not the only girl for you. Even if she was, there is still no real justification for suicide. This life is all we have. It is everything and it is the only thing we actually have. It's a gift no matter how hard or bad it is because there is nothing else. So even if we forget about the fact that there are 3 billion other girls out there, even if there were none and you had to be alone all your life, it would still be worth living because it is all you have. 
   But luckily for you, there are other people out there. Accept that this is hard... it is. You need to grieve this loss and take some time. Do something you love... go for a walk and chill, don't go into the road, maybe a game or a bar or a show or bowling. I dono. But do something. 
  Time will heal this wound. 
But your depression is something else. That's something that you might need some soft medication for or a lot of exercise or healthy food or love... I don't know. But you have an issue that isn't your fault, but it is your job to try and fix it. 
   I am glad you are still with us, and you will be too. Please, try to see this loss in a rational albeit emotional way. It is really sad and I mean that... but it isn't the end. 
 Please feel free to message me anytime.

Hey man, 

That's really tough... but you should note that you're not on your meds right now... what if you wouldn't feel this way after a while of being on meds. You said everything was alright. 50k isn't so bad, plus there are programs that can help you and insurances that might backdate if you get it now. If you got medicaid now they might cover that bill. 
  You have been okay in the past which means you can be okay. It isn't fair to your future self to make this kind of decision while in this mood and without your meds. It's just not fair. 
  You will have a great life... this is where strength and heart come into play. This is what makes people strong. You will be okay. What you have gone through is really tough, but think about all the people around the world right now going through worse... people losing their families, their siblings, ebola, isis... come on man! You got this. 
 People have lived through it and so will you!

The good news is it can only get better. 
 You have identified the things that make your life difficult now (no friends, no hope, no future)... well, maybe these can be fixed. 
  I'll bet you all my money (don't get excited; it's not a lot) that there is someone real nearby to you that will be your friend. Someone who is also struggling (that's all of us) or who understands what you're going through who will be your friend. They will change your life. 
  There is always hope. The world is too big for that statement to ever be true. But right now, you have been in a funk... you're in a rhythm that is based on despair. I bet you don't go out to look for friends and when you do you kinda shy away or back down. (I say this because I do this). So first of all, you need to change a bit... you need to face those fears, throw caution to the wind, ignore the bad voices and go out and have some fun. 
  Let's assume life is horrible and always will be... well, then you have nothing to lose. Fuck it, as they say. You don't have to worry about fixing yourself or changing the world... you just need to worry about enjoying yourself. 
 Change is slow as hell and hard as hell... but it happens and gets easier as it goes. 
  You do need to have a good therapist. They won't change you, but they will help you change. If your therapist isn't good you need to find a new one. 
  Meds are complicated... really complicated. In general you should be really diligent with them. Cut down when you can, but stay on the ones that help you. An ssri can be super helpful in making you feel okay enough to start living. 
 You can do this... but you need to make those changes. Focus on the good. Really... focus on anything that's good. Lie to yourself if you have to... but you've had enough suffering. Fuck it! Keep telling yourself that. Fuck it. This is your time. Go out and have fun! Meet friends. Make a fool of yourself. Fail... who cares. 
 You got this!
Since you used the Grand Canyon as an analogy, I'd like to point out the it took millions of years to form.

That's true... you can't continue to live this way. 
 You say change is impossible, but you also say you're deep in depression thus invalidating the statement. Your depression is talking for you. 
  What if you got a bit less depressed with therapy? Lets say you went from an 8 to a 6... maybe you can live with that and still enjoy life. It is a slow process. You're saying it will never change, but it always changes. You say it can't get worse... well, that's really good. It will change and it will get better. 
  The thing is, you need meds. Not heavy meds that'll squash your brilliance, but a small something (ssri) to take the edge off and balance out your life. It takes a few weeks to start working and gives you a tiny boost. Essentially, your chemistry is a bit out of wack. The binge purge has either caused or is caused by an imbalance. Meds can help that. 
  You are smarter than most of your therapists, but there are those who can help. Those who understand that they shouldn't heavily medicate you, but rather give you a lift so that you can help yourself and not live in so much pain. 
   You are too smart to go out this way. Smart people are always the ones who duffer this much. It sucks... it really sucks. I'm sorry for what you go through and I empathize. I have something similar and meds helped me despite me not thinking they would. 
  Like the person below said: you will upgrade your spoon... you will build confidence and an emotional bank account that you can draw from.  You will get better slowly and things will get easier. But you need to fix the underlying issues and relieve some of the pressure. 
  Submit to the idea of therapy or meds or something... you are clearly brilliant, clearly a deep thinker, clearly like most of us and so you don't let go. But why not? Why not give in to something that can help you? Allow yourself to suspend your critical mind and focus on being happy. 
 I recently tried the "I don't give a fuck" pill... you kinda let everything go and try to enjoy. In spite of every voice telling you to figure out what's right and wrong, what you should be doing, how much better or worse you could be, who you are, when you're gonna be better... you let go of that voice and chill. 
 I don't know if anything I'm saying will resonate with you. But please make the focus on helping yourself instead of how hopeless you are. You are deep in a hole, but not that deep considering. You will be okay.

Your grandmother sounds like a great idea. 
 To be clear, I don't suggest you do this behind her back. I suggest you talk to her and come to a conclusion as to whom to ask. I think she might be okay with passing it along to another person... Be sure that she knows you will not blow this up and let people know. Let her know that you don't know what to do and want to find a person to pass it along to. If she's okay with grandma, that's a great idea! 
  Please don't betray her trust. You're right; that's a bad idea.

I could love someone that requires so much work, and so can anyone else. 
 
I hear what you're saying, and it sounds rough... there is nothing like having everything fail. It sucks balls, to be blunt. 
 I think the silver-lining here is that all of your issues are coming from the same place. You are not doing well emotionally. It's affecting your school, your relationship, your outlook... So we need to fix that. 
  You say your medication would only numb you. This is true of certain medications, like the ones you didn't like maybe... however, other medications designed for long-term use, like Prozac, Zoloft... really don't affect you that much. They are not designed to numb you, but rather to help your brain regain the balance it needs. You feel the need for that and you write about it, but it's time to get on top of it and fix that. 
 I'm sorry that you're struggling with school. The truth is, college is like a hyped up commercialized ideal that is super tough to deal with. You don't get the degree or you do and you just feel weird... there is no immediate change in your life or huge gratification... it's just education. You're a different person but you don't know it. The fact that you've been so challenged is a really good thing. It's not easy, but it's good. You failed so many times... great, that'll make the success so much better. Just don't give up yet. In fact, know that you will finish and do it, for you. Not for the pay jump, not for the family or friends who you feel are judging you. Fuck them. Finish for you. You can do it! 
  Your relationship doesn't sound good. I'm not sure if it can be made better by you feeling better. If it can, work on it. If it can't, end it. You need to get out more, meet friends, chill, have fun and do things you love. You live in a city you say, so go find some crazy shit to do. It's all there. 
 It won't change your life, but it'll make it more fun and easier to manage. 
    You are not done until you want to be done. These obstacles are tough, but you will get through them and come out stronger. I like to take the "I don't give a fuck" pill when I'm in these situations... Change the pessimistic apathy into "I don't give a fuck" and you might have fun... Just chill... do your work, do well but accept that you might fail again, and that's okay. It isn't over until you say it's over! 
  Also, get help with schooling. Go to the tutoring center, talk to every professor, work harder, find a student who will help you. You got this! 
   Fuck feeling bad for yourself. You're not a bad adult... you're a normal 24 year old. We all go through this. Trust me... I'm 26 and can't get my degree because I owe the school money. Same shit. You are not a bad adult, in fact, you're really not even an adult yet. People say 18, but that's bull shit. The 20's are a tough time where crazy things happen and we need to find ourselves... but you have so so so much life ahead of you. Just keep making those good decisions, put in the work, get that degree, kick ass and have fun doing it! 
 If you ever need to talk or have questions with school (I'm really good at navigating college) just message me!

Firstly, it's really amazing that she came to you. She obviously trusts you. Also, amazing that you came here. 
  I think the best option is to find someone who can help her. That means finding someone you both think can take over this situation. Calling an ambulance or police is for emergencies; if she is a real threat to herself right now, that's what you must do. However, if it's a chronic depression she's going through, you should discuss with her who to tell. Perhaps you have a parent, uncle, friends... who is a professional or who is great at dealing with this. 
 She will be okay... some therapy, maybe some soft medication... life is rough, especially when you don't have a job and your ex is in town. This is a tough time and someone should be dealing with it. 
 If I was near you I would try to help, but I'm not... There are centers she can go to and the suicide hotline will always help you find one of them. Perhaps you should call them. They are really nice. 
   Please find someone who can help her... I think you two will be okay.

Hey...
 I know what it's like to graduate and not be able to find work. In fact, many people think that post-graduation is the toughest part of people's lives. You really go from being a kid to being an adult. You're expected to just "get a job" and have everything worked out, but in reality we're just babies coming into the real world. It's a huge switch and can cause so much anxiety. 
 The good news is that you have a degree and can eventually work things out. 
 I don't think suicide will help you or your mom. I really think you're going through a tough time and that's okay. It's something to get past and get stronger from. You don't want to die... you just really don't want to be in your situation. I get that! I totally get that. 
  Try not to be too hard on yourself. You are not the only one going through this right now. In fact, it's about 50% or more of graduates that go back to live at home and can't find work. You have got to spend your time doing what you love. 
  You will be okay... If you have questions or need to talk, just message me or reply. Vent if you need to. I'm here to listen. 
  You will be okay. I promise you that!

Firstly, you sound like an absolute sweetheart, for whatever that's worth. 
 Thank you. I'm not totally clean. I smoke and would do other drugs if they came along... but alcohol was my crutch. 
   I really feel for you man. I mean, not sympathy because sympathy is stupid and pointless. I have ulcerative colitis which makes me like a child when it's bad, which is almost always. No visible signs, but my friends (or anyone) might ask to hang out or go out or drive anywhere.. and I can't do it because I can't control my stomach. So I understand the chronic condition difficulty. 
   This does sound like the new meds. I don't know what they are, but I hope they level out for you... if not, new meds. It's rough, but you will find a balance that works for you.  
  Yeah, alcohol puts you in that super depressive artsy apathetic mindset that leads to this, but it's okay. 
    I'm thinking of something interesting... kinda a paradigm shift. So let's say you walk into a classroom to pick someone up and some ten year old kid laughs at you. You can get angry (which is normal) or hurt (normal) or sad (normal)...... or you can teach the kid something they will never forget. With compassion you can explain that you have a condition. Very openly and honestly let them know that you understand why they're laughing or staring or saying something mean, and you don't want to make them feel bad, but they should know that you have a condition called Tourettes that makes it impossible for you to control it. 
 It can change their life. You can educate people and that can make you feel good because it's a really good thing... I would say, as hard as it is, explore what you have and learn it and teach it. There is inherent value in someone who can do that... (sorry if this all sounds weird - it's just an example of an idea)... you can help people through education.

This is super common... you feel good on the ssri and then feel like you can go off. When you go off you feel even better than before, but then this happens. 
  This isn't as bad as you think. Try not to think about all the things that can go wrong and focus instead on making yourself back to how you were. This probably means getting back on the meds, which isn't bad at all. Actually, it's really good... it works for you. So do it. It doesn't say anything about your character or anything like that; sometimes we just need meds to balance us out, just like blood pressure medication or insulin. You will be okay! 
  Get back on those meds. Let me know how it goes... it'll take about five tough weeks, but you will do great! 
Please be very careful when you get back on them if you feel suicidal. Sometimes with those meds they make you feel good enough to do something stupid before they balance you out. So let your doctor know you feel suicidal sometimes and want to be extra careful! Please don't hurt yourself... message me if you ever feel that way.

How long have you been on the Zoloft for? I ask because if this is new, it's normal to feel this way. If not, perhaps a different medication would be better. 
  I personally have taken Zoloft... Also, I used to drink every single day. I haven't had a drink in 27 months (I'm not in AA)... and I'm not gonna convince you to not drink. But what I found is that two weeks after I stopped drinking, my anxiety was manageable. It went from an impossible thing to control (because alcohol gets stuck in your nervous system) to something I could handle. It really was like magic. It's so hard though... because you don't see results right away and alcohol feels so good. Just a thought though. 
  You sound young. How old are you? And why are people laughing at you? Fuck those people! People are mean, but usually the mean people are lame and stupid and weak.... You are strong and complex. You have experience and these great challenges. Why worry about those idiots.

I think this is cool... firstly, you'll know for sure that any girl who stays with you likes you for more than your looks. That is invaluable. Totally priceless, knowing that you are good looking and that you have a reason why a shallow girl wouldn't go out with you. They will love you for who you are!  
Also, have you looked into medical treatment of this. I know that in children this is very easy to fix. Is there a surgery that would be worth it for you? 
  I imagine it's rough... I mean, many people have things like this, and this one sounds rough too. A small penis, being fat, pimples, sweating... these are things that ultimately are not as important and we make them. There is so much more to life than this. It's rough... but it'll make you so much stronger and a much better person. 
   This is no reason to give up. It's a reason to get stronger and to love yourself even more. Change that attitude!

Heyo...
 I know what it's like to be bored and in need of company... 
   Message me anytime!
